thread:
Lucy_Acme: hey, we're seeing a bunch of 502s + timeouts hitting /v1/generate from our production pool since ~10:12 UTC. non-streaming requests, concurrency ~40. sample curl returned 502 + 'upstream reset'. request id: req-2387.

Jenna_Support: ack, sorry about that — can you paste the exact X-Request-Id header value and an example curl/python snippet you used? also which SDK version are you on and are you doing retries client-side?

Lucy_Acme: request id is req-2387. SDK version 1.2.3. we do naive retry on 5xx with no jitter, timeout 30s. example: ```python
resp = client.generate("...")
# 40 concurrent workers via ThreadPoolExecutor
```

Mike_SRE: thanks. pinging infra — I'm seeing connection resets from an edge node in usw2 at 10:11-10:20 in our aggregated logs. can you confirm if your token rotation is happening around that time? also any streaming vs non-streaming differences?

Lucy_Acme: no token rotation on our side during that window. all non-streaming. i can repro locally by hammering with the same concurrency, will paste results soon.

Samir_SDK: fyi SDK 1.2.3 has an http2 connection reuse issue we patched in 1.2.4-beta — in some cases the client reuses a conn after token refresh and server rejects with connection-reset. try upgrade or force HTTP/1.1 as workaround. repro snippet (python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., http_version="1.1")
def call():
  return client.generate("hello")
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=50) as e:
  list(e.map(call, range(100)))
```

Lucy_Acme: ran a quick run with 50 concurrent, got ~5/50 requests 502 with 'connection reset by peer' in client stack. paste from logs: ```ERROR: httpx._exceptions.RemoteProtocolError: unexpected EOF while reading HTTP/2 stream```

oncall-bot: [ALERT] spike: 502-count > 5% for host redwood-gateway-usw2 between 10:11:30 and 10:18:45 — deploy id: dpl-9043, svc: api-gateway (investigate) :eyes:

Mike_SRE: rolling a temporary routing change to avoid the suspect edge node (dpl-9043). can you bump client timeout to 60s and add exponential backoff + jitter for retries while we investigate? that should reduce duplicate work and billing churn.

Jenna_Support: lucy, would it be ok if we enable a temporary per-customer burst quota so your jobs don't backpressure and spike retries while we cut over the node? also we'll mark this P1 internal.

Lucy_Acme: yes please enable the burst, thanks. also worried about billing — our retry loop might double-charge token usage. can you confirm whether failed 502 attempts are billed?

Samir_SDK: short answer: tokens may be counted for requests that reached the generation backend before failing; we log ingest rates and token consumption separately. long answer we can send to billing, but as mitigation upgrade SDK (1.2.4+) which reduces spurious retries and handles auth rehandshake correctly. doc: https://redwood.example/docs/sdk-releases (internal)

Mike_SRE: root cause summary: token-refresh + HTTP/2 conn reuse bug on client (1.2.3) led to stale auth on reused streams, upstream closed connection -> gateway 502s. action taken: rolled routing away from the affected edge node, restarted a subset of edge proxies, enabled sticky reconnection, and applied hotfix to edge auth validation so stale streams get 401 rather than silent reset.

Mike_SRE: ask: please upgrade SDK to 1.2.4 (or set http_version=1.1) and add jittered exponential backoff. we'll keep the temporary burst enabled for 2 hours.

Lucy_Acme: upgraded to 1.2.4 and re-ran the same concurrent test (100 requests) — 0/100 failed, no 502s. thanks for the fast triage. please keep the burst for 30 more mins and then you can close.

Jenna_Support: great to hear. I'll leave the burst for 30 mins and close this thread after monitoring. follow-up: we'll open a billing review for any disputed token charges during the window — you'll get a note from billing@ within the hour.

Lucy_Acme: thanks everyone :heart:, please tag me in the billing thread. closing after monitoring.

Mike_SRE: noted — closing on our side once metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
